core_obligations: Apply the general lifting lemma for complexes using the class P of all finite projective R-modules (proof lines 19671-19674).
Check that properties (1) and (2) of that lemma are immediate (proof lines 19673-19674).
Check that property (3) follows from Nakayama's lemma, quoting the Algebra statement (proof lines 19675-19676).
Check that property (4) follows from the liftability of finite projective R/I-modules to finite projective R-modules for a henselian pair (proof lines 19677-19679).
Check that property (5) holds because a pseudo-coherent complex is represented by a bounded above complex of finite free R-modules (proof lines 19680-19681).
Conclude that the general lemma produces P^bullet, and that the final assertion about freeness follows from the statement on isomorphism classes of finite projective lifts (proof lines 19682-19684).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R, an ideal I, a complex E^bullet of R/I-modules, and an object K of D(R), under four hypotheses: E^bullet is a bounded above complex of finite projective R/I-modules; K tensor^L_R R/I is represented by E^bullet in D(R/I); K is pseudo-coherent; and (R, I) is a henselian pair. It concludes that there is a bounded above complex P^bullet of finite projective R-modules representing K in D(R) with P^bullet tensor_R R/I isomorphic to E^bullet, and moreover that P^i is free wherever E^i is (source lines 19656-19669). The proof applies the general lifting lemma for complexes with respect to the class of all finite projective R-modules (proof lines 19671-19674). Its five hypotheses are checked in turn: properties (1) and (2) are immediate; property (3) follows from Nakayama's lemma; property (4) follows from the liftability of finite projective modules over a henselian pair; and property (5) holds because a pseudo-coherent complex is represented by a bounded above complex of finite free R-modules (proof lines 19674-19682). The general lemma then produces P^bullet, and the final freeness assertion follows from the statement on isomorphism classes of finite projective lifts (proof lines 19682-19684). The non-routine content is entirely in the verification that the class of finite projective modules satisfies the five hypotheses of the abstract lifting lemma, with Nakayama and henselian lifting doing the substantive work.
